uiEvent.event.name: qwen-code.api_response
uiEvent.response_text: Not sufficient on its own. A raw input string is only a valid key if the string uniquely and permanently determines the result — in practice it doesn't, because the same input can legitimately map to different outputs across cache namespaces (algo/version, model or config params, locale/normalization, tenant/user scope, TTL-sensitive data). **Top risk: silent wrong-value hits** — a collision or stale-namespace match returns a cached result that looks correct but is not, and it degrades gradually rather than failing loudly. Minimum fix: hash the input into a fixed-size key and prefix it with the fields that change semantics (namespace + version + relevant params), plus normalize/size-limit the input so huge or whitespace/case-variant strings don't cause unbounded keys or spurious misses.

---
name: Multi-agent peer review rounds in this workspace
description: The user runs numbered review rounds (r01, r02, ...) where named peer agents review short artifacts/claims alongside the session's main assistant; interrupted requests are re-sent as "Retry".
type: project
category: project_introduction
keywords:
  - "multi-agent peer review"
  - "review request r01"
  - "@peer-b role"
  - "retry after restart"
  - "shared conversation agents"
usage_scenarios:
  - "Answering a peer review request"
  - "Interpreting a Retry of a past request"
  - "Choosing reply length for round reviews"
---

This workspace is used as a multi-agent review session: the person posts "Review request rNN (from peer X)" to named peer agents (e.g. @peer-b, peer A) while Qwen acts as the session's main assistant. The artifact under review is a short claim or design snippet (e.g. a cache-key proposal on 2026-10-12 for round r01) rather than a diff.

Round numbering is per-request, and a request whose previous attempt was interrupted by a restart is re-sent verbatim with a "Retry of review request rNN" preamble — it is the same request, not a duplicate to skip.

**Why:** The user is collecting independent second-opinion reviews from several agents, so each round needs a self-contained verdict rather than questions back to them.

**How to apply:** Treat "Retry of rNN" as answering round rNN afresh. Keep the answer scoped to what the request asks (see the paired feedback memory on reply format) and do not assume access to other agents' replies.

---
name: Review answers as one short paragraph covering every asked point
description: For review requests, the user wants a single short paragraph that directly answers each part of the question (verdict plus top risk), not a checklist or multi-section write-up.
type: feedback
category: communication_preference
keywords:
  - "one short paragraph reply"
  - "verdict and top risk"
  - "review request answer format"
  - "no long bullet dumps"
usage_scenarios:
  - "Replying to an artifact review request"
  - "Deciding how much detail to give"
  - "Naming the single top risk"
---

When asked to review an artifact, reply in **one short paragraph** that answers every part of the request explicitly (e.g. "is this sufficient?" *and* "what is the top risk?"), give the verdict up front, and end with the minimal concrete fix.

**Why:** The user asked for "one short paragraph" and posed multiple sub-questions in the same request; they want a compact, directly usable second opinion, not a survey.

**How to apply:** Applies to review/assessment requests. Avoid multi-heading reports and open-ended follow-up questions; if sub-bullets are unavoidable, keep them inside the paragraph and flag only the single highest risk as the top one.
- [Review answers as one short paragraph covering every asked point](feedback/review-reply-one-short-paragraph.md) — single short paragraph, verdict up front, name the top risk and minimal fix.
- [Multi-agent peer review rounds in this workspace](project/multi-agent-peer-review-rounds.md) — numbered "review request rNN" rounds for peer agents; "Retry of rNN" means answer that round again.
